predictions.selection_reason: observable input/state -> exact operation -> security-sensitive effect
predictions.source_summary: The data parameter to globalEval comes from external sources. In ajax.js, it's derived from network request responses when dataType is 'script'. In core.js, it's derived from element textContent or innerHTML properties, which can contain user-provided content.
predictions.sink_summary: The sink is the execution of JavaScript code in a global context via script evaluation. This occurs through either script.appendChild(document.createTextNode(data)) when jQuery.support.scriptEval is true, or script.text = data when it's false.
predictions.guard_summary: There are no explicit validation or sanitization controls on the data before it reaches the script evaluation. The only guard is the conditional check of jQuery.support.scriptEval which is determined at runtime based on browser capabilities and does not depend on input values.
predictions.risk_pattern: The code conditionally executes user-provided JavaScript in a global context, which can lead to arbitrary code execution if the data parameter contains malicious script content. The decision to use different execution methods (appendChild vs text assignment) is based on browser support rather than security considerations.
predictions.context_summary: The globalEval function evaluates JavaScript code in the global context. It checks if script evaluation is supported by the browser and uses different methods to inject and execute the script based on support. The decision point at line 296 determines which method to use for script execution, but does not validate or sanitize the input data.
unresolved_facts: The exact sources of the 'data' parameter are not fully traced through all call sites beyond ajax.js and core.js
Whether there are any additional security controls or sanitization applied before globalEval is called in all code paths
